meta.se_formula: sqrt(4/80 * sum_r (x_r - x)^2) over the 80 successive-difference replicate weights; derived statistics (ratios, differences, logs) are evaluated on every replicate

universes.all: all workers with a US POWPUMA of residence and of work
universes.metro_pow: residents of metropolitan areas: residence POWPUMA class city or suburb (rows city and suburb of the matrix)
universes.metro_puma: residents of metropolitan PUMAs: residence PUMA class city or suburb (the `metro` flag of the commute block of teacher_residence.py), cells on the POWPUMA classes
universes.away: workers who work away from home (JWTR != 11)

groups.all: employed persons 16+ with a US POWPUMA of residence and of work
groups.nonteacher: all of the above except OCCP 2310-2330 (elementary/middle, secondary and special-education teachers; OCCP 2300 preschool/kindergarten teachers stay in)
groups.k12: OCCP 2310-2330 (`k12` of teacher_residence.py), recomputed here as a check on the code
groups.pub_k12: OCCP 2310-2330 employed by a local or state government (COW 3-4), recomputed as a check

meta.layout: groups.<group>.universes.<universe>: res[a], work[b], x['a->b'] (joint shares), work_given_live[a][b] = P(work b | live a), live_given_work[b][a] = P(live a | work b), p_work_suburb_given_live_city, p_work_city_given_live_suburb, share_cross_city_suburb, share_cross_class, gap_res, gap_work, net_commute_gap, block{share_of_group, city_share_jobs, city_share_residents, net_inflow_to_city}, marginal{city_share_residents, city_share_jobs}, n_sample, n_cells, workers_millions; each statistic is {value, se}. differences.<universe>.<group>_minus_nonteacher.<statistic>; class_cuts[i].groups.<group>; headline = the main statistics of groups.<group>.universes.all and .metro_pow
methods: Data and sample: the ACS 2018 1-year PUMS cached by teacher_residence.py (employed persons 16+, ESR 1-2, in households; 80 replicate weights), restricted as in its `flows_block` to persons with a US place-of-work POWPUMA (POWSP 1-56, POWPUMA > 1). Workers at home carry their own POWPUMA as the place of work (checked: all of them do), so they count as working where they live; persons employed but not at work last week and workplaces abroad or in Puerto Rico are out.

Classes: `teacher_residence.build_puma_geo()` at the main cut (0.5 / 0.5): a POWPUMA is `city` if at least half of its 2010 population lives in principal cities of OMB (Sept. 2018) metropolitan areas, `suburb` if at least half lives in metropolitan counties and it is not `city`, `other` otherwise. Residence class = class of the POWPUMA that contains the residence PUMA; workplace class = class of the place-of-work POWPUMA (one geography at both ends).

Groups: all workers; non-teachers = everyone except OCCP 2310-2330 (the `k12` flag of teacher_residence.py). K-12 and public K-12 (COW 3-4) teachers are recomputed by the same code as a check and reproduce `flows.k12` / `flows.pub_k12` of teacher_residence.json.

Estimator: person-weighted cell shares; every probability is a ratio of cells. Standard errors from the 80 ACS replicate weights, SE = sqrt(4/80 sum_r (x_r - x)^2), with derived statistics and between-group differences evaluated on every replicate (covariances respected). Sampling error only.

Definitions: `block` = workers who live AND work in a city or suburb POWPUMA (the closed two-location system); crossing share = (city->suburb + suburb->city) / block (`share_metro_cross` of teacher_residence.py); `marginal` = workers who live (work) in a city or suburb POWPUMA, whatever the other end. Caveat: a POWPUMA is a whole county or group of counties, so city-suburb commuting inside one county is invisible and the crossing probabilities are lower bounds; workers at home count as non-crossers (see `away`); the classes depend on the cuts (`class_cuts`).
